name: seizures overview
title: First seizure: history decides whether it was a seizure, then whether it was provoked; for an unprovoked seizure, MRI and EEG estimate the recurrence risk, which decides between discussing treatment for a single seizure and recommending it for epilepsy; drug-resistant epilepsy goes to an epilepsy centre; status epilepticus is an emergency

root.title: A first seizure: HISTORY is the key
lines: details of the event · witnesses · ambulance records · risk factors: febrile seizures, head trauma, meningitis or encephalitis, family history
URGENT evaluation if fever, trauma, enduring confusion or low consciousness, or a persistent focal deficit

groups.title: UNPROVOKED: how likely is ANOTHER?
lines: an enduring abnormality: genetic, old stroke, old trauma, tumour

pres.title: Work up to estimate the RECURRENCE RISK
lines: 1 · electrolytes (extended) · CT in the emergency department: bleed, tumour?
2 · MRI, epilepsy protocol: a STRUCTURAL lesion ↑ risk
